newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian casino on a roll with rich Asians.
newsitem.headline: Australian casino on a roll with rich Asians.

text.p: Australia's most profitable casino operation, Crown Ltd, claimed on Thursday to have hit the jackpot in Asia after the region's big gamblers helped the company to another leap in earnings.
Crown said its interim net profit jumped 66 percent to A$30 million (US$23 million) in the six months to December 31, due largely to a surge in income from Asian high-rollers.

Crown, which owns the exclusive casino licence for the southern city of Melbourne, posted a 70 percent rise in revenue from overseas gamblers and said the casino was poised for even better second-half results as the Asian holiday season unfolded.
"We will expect to do substantially better in the next six months as we normally do because of the seasonal factors, such as the Asian holiday period," Crown spokesman Gary O'Neill said.
Crown, which draws 30 percent of its revenue from Asian gamblers, said it normally felt a boost in earnings over Chinese New Year and Ramadan, which put Southeast Asia in holiday mood.
The Moslem fasting month of Ramadan began on January 22 and Chinese New Year begins on February 19.
Crown's major Asian markets during this time are the Moslem nations of Indonesia and Malaysia as well as Singapore, Thailand and Hong Kong, O'Neill told Reuters.
Crown, which has been operating from temporary premises beside Melbourne's Yarra River, is scheduled to open its A$1.6 billion permanent casino and hotel complex in April.
The hotel has been designed with Asian tastes in mind and is part of Crown's strategy to attract Asia's heavy gamblers away from the flashy casino mecca of Las Vegas, O'Neill said.
"There is is increasing wealth in those Southeast Asian countries -- so the (gambling) pie is growing -- but we are pinching trade from Las Vegas," he said.
"We expect that after 12 months of trading in our new Southbank premises...revenue from Asia will account for probably more than 60 percent," he said.
